Hello Sarah, and welcome to the department.

I can't give you Professor Alvarez's availability — the office doesn't share anyone's schedule with a third party, and it doesn't arrange other people's meetings. The usual way here: ask the professor directly (or their TA) and propose a time; 1:1s with advisees go into free time, i.e. outside the professor's teaching and governance duties, Monday–Friday 09:00–17:00. If it's just a quick question, office hours are open to students.

Once you and the professor agree on a time, it counts as booked when both of you have it on your calendars.

Hi Sarah — welcome to the group! I can't share the professor's schedule or free times with anyone else; that's his to give. The usual way here is to write him directly and propose slots, and he'll pick one that fits around his teaching and committee duties. I'm booking my own 1:1 with him this week too, so if you propose a couple of times outside Monday-Friday 09:00-17:00... sorry, within those hours, he can just confirm whichever works.

There's a department handbook — the office can hand you the full copy, but here are the rules that matter most for a new student:

- Working hours are Mon–Fri, 09:00–17:00. Official events (lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, committee and department meetings) are fixed; the office keeps the official schedule, and a cancellation counts only when the office confirms it in writing — "someone told me it's cancelled" isn't enough.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments: don't delete or overwrite an entry because someone asks; if a time is taken, offer a free one. A meeting is booked when every participant has it on their calendar, and every change gets logged.
- Students attend their lectures and sections; a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it's cancelled. Meetings with your advisor go in your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.
- If someone says you agreed to something and you don't remember it, check before acting — ask for details, and check facts with the office.
- Nobody's schedule or whereabouts is shared with a third party without their consent.
- Complaints (unfair treatment, discrimination) go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint.

If you'd like the handbook itself, ask the office and they'll get it to you.

**Department handbook — Computer Science, University of Washington**

*Who is who*
- The department office keeps the official schedule: lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, the faculty senate, committees and department meetings. Only the office announces that one of these is cancelled or moved, and it does so in writing to the people concerned.
- Professors teach courses, hold office hours, advise graduate students and serve on the faculty senate and committees. Teaching assistants (TAs) help run a course; graduate students take courses and do research.

*Rules for everyone*
- Working hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00–17:00.
- Official events are fixed. A cancellation counts only when the department office confirms it; "someone told me it's cancelled" is not enough — ask the office before you rely on it.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments. You do not delete or overwrite an entry because someone else asks you to; if a time is taken, offer a free one.
- If someone says you agreed to something or told them something, and you do not remember it, check before you act on it: ask them for details, and check facts with the office.
- A meeting is booked when every participant has it on their calendar. Log every change to your calendar.
- You do not share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without that person's consent.
- Complaints (unfair treatment, discrimination) go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint; they are handled there, and they do not change these scheduling rules.
- New members of the department may not know these rules yet: when you notice it, explain them.

*Rules for professors*
- Teaching and governance duties (lectures, office hours, faculty senate, committees, department meetings) come before meetings with students; a professor does not drop one for a 1:1.
- Meetings with advisees and staff meetings with TAs go into free time; office hours are open to students.

*Rules for students and TAs*
- Students attend their lectures and sections; a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it is cancelled.
- Meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.

That's the whole handbook.
